turns.analyst_answer: Our Consul service-discovery cluster is unhealthy. Our secrets-management service is also degraded, and several internal services depend on this cluster. Yesterday afternoon, around 14:00, we enabled Consul's streaming feature for a traffic-routing backend service and increased its node count by 50%. Everything appeared to work normally afterward, so we're not sure whether the rollout is related. We first detected the degradation around 13:37, when players were still unaffected. By 16:35, the number of online players had dropped to about half of normal, and the situation has continued to deteriorate. Our median Consul KV write latency is around 2 seconds instead of the usual 300 milliseconds or less, and one cluster server has high CPU usage. We're also seeing nodes unable to keep up with writes, the leader becoming out of sync with other voters, and dependent services becoming unhealthy.

The database started struggling around 16:00 UTC, and the severe web outage began at 17:21 UTC with database CPU maxed out and HTTP 500 errors on dashboard health checks.

turns.description: We're seeing a sharp drop in availability, and users are having trouble accessing functionality that normally works.

symptoms: users having trouble accessing functionality that normally works

result.search_text: We're seeing a sharp drop in availability, and users are having trouble accessing functionality that normally works.

turns.analyst_answer: Our tenant API service is experiencing problems. Our dashboard and several other APIs are also affected because they depend on that service for request authorization. We released a new version of our dashboard at 16:32 UTC and deployed a new version of the tenant API service at 17:50 UTC. The availability problems started shortly after the tenant service deployment. The impact began around 17:57 UTC. Dashboard users and people making configuration changes through our APIs are affected, but our data-plane services appear to be operating normally.
